hook: Apple TV’s secret Soviet base hides a ten‑episode twist.

sections.voiceover: Apple TV’s secret Soviet base hides a ten‑episode twist.
sections.visual_cue: A shadowy Soviet training facility with a bold "10 episodes" overlay.
b_roll: archival footage of Star City training grounds

sections.voiceover: In October 2026, Reason’s Jason Russell reviewed Apple TV’s Star City. What happened when journalists finally entered Star City in 1997?
sections.visual_cue: Timeline graphic: Oct 2026 → show cover, then ten‑episode badge, then 1997 newspaper headline.
sections.sfx_cue: typewriter clicks, then a ticking clock
b_roll: Reason magazine cover featuring Star City
1997 newspaper clipping of journalists at Star City

sections.voiceover: Yet TV veterans Ben Nedivi, Matt Wolpert, and Ronald D. Moore created it.
sections.visual_cue: Portraits of the three creators appear side‑by‑side with a director’s clapboard.
b_roll: behind‑the‑scenes photo of the production team

sections.voiceover: The ten‑episode series shows KGB overseers turning cosmonaut training into a surveillance nightmare. Recruits endured loyalty tests, and dissent vanished without a trace. When journalists entered Star City in 1997, they exposed that chilling reality.
sections.visual_cue: Montage: KGB officers watching trainees, a locked file labeled "loyalty tests", then 1997 press badge flashing.
b_roll: close‑up of a stamped loyalty test document
news footage of 1997 journalists at the base

sections.voiceover: A ten‑episode glimpse into Soviet paranoia finally revealed.
sections.visual_cue: Final title card: "10 episodes – Soviet Paranoia" with fading starfield.
b_roll: starry night sky over the Kremlin silhouette
